content.text:
I have enough evidence to conclude.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b12a8a63db38dcdb3b93503fe9f3552bc341a87d

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation.** The fix (f5c417c7) re-adds a single line in `CrossflowHandler.java`'s `startExperiment` method: `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);`, right after the `Workflow` instance is constructed via reflection using a custom `URLClassLoader` built from the experiment's jar. I traced the history of this line and of `Serializer.setClassloader`/`CrossflowHandler.java` using `git log -p --follow`.

**(2) The change that introduced the bug.** The call `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader)` was originally introduced back in commit `1849376f` (Dec 2018) and persisted through many commits. Commit **`b12a8a63`** ("Tue Jul 23 2019") is a large rewrite/reformat of `CrossflowHandler.java` that, among whitespace changes, did two substantive things:
- Changed the workflow instantiation to `classLoader.loadClass(...).getConstructor(Mode.class, ClassLoader.class).newInstance(mode, classLoader)` (passing the classloader into a two-arg constructor), and
- **Removed** the explicit `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);` line, apparently assuming the (nonexistent) two-arg `Workflow(Mode, ClassLoader)` constructor would handle wiring the classloader into the serializer itself.

I verified via `git log -p --all -- '*.egl'` that none of the Crossflow code-generation templates (which generate the `Workflow` subclasses) ever define a `Workflow(Mode, ClassLoader)` constructor — it never existed. So the `getConstructor(Mode.class, ClassLoader.class)` call introduced in `b12a8a63` would throw `NoSuchMethodException` at runtime, and crucially, the serializer's classloader was never set anywhere.

Two days later, commit `a6b23429` reverted the broken reflective call back to `getConstructor(Mode.class).newInstance(mode)` (fixing the `NoSuchMethodException`), but its diff touches **only** that one line — it does not restore the `setClassloader` call. So from `b12a8a63` onward, the custom `URLClassLoader` built for the experiment's jar was created but never actually applied to the XStream-based `Serializer`, meaning classes from the uploaded experiment jar could not be correctly resolved during (de)serialization.

**(3) Supporting evidence.**
- `git show b12a8a63 -- CrossflowHandler.java` shows the removal of `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);` in the same commit that also changed the constructor lookup.
- `git show a6b23429 -- CrossflowHandler.java` shows a minimal, isolated diff (only the `getConstructor(...)` line), confirming it did not touch/restore the serializer line — it only fixed the unrelated reflection-signature regression.
- `Serializer.java`'s `setClassloader` method (added in `1849376f`, unchanged since) exists solely to propagate a custom classloader into the internal `XStream` instance, confirming its purpose and that it was simply orphaned (never called) after `b12a8a63`.
- The fix commit `f5c417c7` does exactly one thing: reinstates that exact call, consistent with "the call was dropped and needs restoring" rather than any new feature.

I'm highly confident `b12a8a63` is the bug-introducing commit, since it's the exact point where the `setClassloader` call was deleted and never replaced by equivalent functionality. `a6b23429` is a secondary commit in the same short sequence but did not independently introduce or worsen this particular bug (it fixed a different, more severe break caused by the same parent commit).
